tip: Demitir-se means to quit your own job. Drop the se and demitir means to fire someone. Ela se demitiu = she resigned.
Fazer a barba literally means to make the beard, but it is the normal way to say to shave. Eu me cortei fazendo a barba = I cut myself shaving.
Dar-se conta de is a set phrase for to realize or become aware. Nós nos demos conta do erro = we realized the mistake.
A gente means we in casual speech but takes a singular verb like ele. That is why it is se comunica, never comunicam.
Foi preso is passive: ser plus a past participle. Preso agrees with the subject, so a woman would be foi presa.
The o before conheço means him, a direct object pronoun sitting in front of the verb. In speech many say não conheço ele instead.
Apaixonar-se takes por for what you fall for, and por plus o contracts to pelo. Eu me apaixonei pelo Brasil = I fell in love with Brazil.
Há plus a length of time means ago: há cinco anos = five years ago. It comes from haver, not from ter.
Conhecer usually means to know, but with the reciprocal nos it means to meet for the first time. Nós nos conhecemos numa festa = we met at a party.
Divertir-se is reflexive in Portuguese: você se diverte to have fun. Vocês se divertiram na festa = did you enjoy the party.
Quero que forces the subjunctive: the verb becomes leia, not lê. Wanting someone else to act triggers this mood. Quero que ele leia esse livro.
Gostar normally needs de before its object, but when the thing is already clear you can drop it: não gostei = I didn't like it.
Preocupar-se pairs with com for what worries you. A gente se preocupa demais com bobagem = we worry too much over silly things.
In casual Brazilian Portuguese the command uses the ele form: fala, not the textbook fale. Fala mais devagar = speak more slowly.
